lead.headline: 553 water permits broke pollution limits in 36+ of 40 quarters; 84 never had a formal enforcement action
lead.number: 553 permits in 36+ of 40 quarters, 2016-2025; 152 with no formal action since 2016 and 84 with none ever, in EPA's system; in West Virginia, chronic mines got formal action 26% of the time vs 58% for chronic sewer plants.
lead.watch_out: Every count is an absence in EPA's system, and West Virginia's mine enforcement barely flows into it, so "no action" may just mean "not reported."

sources.page_context: hnology Assessments Science & Tech Spotlights Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Related Reports Performance Audits Multimedia Testimonies Presentations Forums & Roundtables Fast Facts The EPA uses National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits to regulate wastewater discharges. However, nearly 11,000 facilities significantly exceeded their permit limits and illegally discharged pollutants into nearby waters in 2018. EPA has a goal to reduce by half significant noncompliance with individual NPDES permits by the end of FY 2022. But the data that states and facilities report to EPA to help track compliance is incomplete and has errors.
